messages:
anya: Heads-up — starting a short thread about the console/analytics storage migration we need to land next week. Key goals: zero-ui-regressions, safe rollback, and minimal query perf impact.
rohan: high level plan?
anya: dual-write -> shadow-read -> canary cutover. But we need concrete gating for quota routing metrics and dashboard p99s.
mike: agree. For dual-write we should record a write-version tag on events so the read adapter can pick the right envelope. Something like `ingest_version = 'v2-metric-envelope'` in the JSON blob.
jess: +1. Also need a short plan for console UX: show a deprecation/compatibility banner when results come from shadow data vs canonical, and hide rollout toggles behind a feature flag.
rohan: Can we surface a per-route mismatch metric? I want a paired count: v1_count vs v2_count per route per minute so we can detect skew.
eva: ingest-bot can emit that if we add a small shim at write time, but cost concerns — sampling at 1% might help early.
mike: Sampling ok, but make sure we keep routes with small cardinality unsampled. Suggest deterministic sample by hash(route_id) % 100 < 1 OR route_event_count < 1000/day.
anja: (typo) — anya: +1 to deterministic sample. Also we should log full diffs for random 100/day route_ids for manual inspection.
jess: For dashboards: create a dashboard card that shows mismatch_ratio = abs(v2_count - v1_count)/max(1,v1_count). Add p50/p95 latency differences. That will help SRE decide rollback.
rohan: Query concern: the new envelope joins add a JSONB->columns projection that could kill p99. Any suggestions?
mike: We can add a materialized projection table populated by the shadow write job. Sync with ingest team to add indexes on (route_id, day). Use TTL async to avoid long-lived small tables.
anya: Rollback plan: (1) stop reads from v2 (read adapter toggles back), (2) mark dual-write off, (3) run a short reconciliation to ensure no drift. Need clear runbook with commands.
rohan: Can we add the exact commands to the runbook now? Example: ```sql -- switch read adapter to prefer v1
UPDATE feature_flags SET value='v1-only' WHERE key='console.ingest.read_mode';
``` and a service toggle: `POST /admin/feature-toggle/console-ingest?mode=v1-only`.
jess: Add a telemetry event on toggles: `telemetry('ingest_migration_toggle', {from:'v2',to:'v1',actor:'...'} )` so product knows when we rolled back.
eva: For canary, propose 5% traffic to v2 for 24h then 20% for 48h, while monitoring mismatch_ratio and dashboard error rates. Abort if mismatch_ratio>0.02 for routes with >1000 events/day.
mike: Also set a hard SLA for query p95 increase: if p95_new / p95_old > 1.25 for console queries, auto-fail the canary. We can implement that in the rollout job.
rohan: We should add a safepoint snapshot: before cutover take a small compact snapshot of routing metadata used by the join keys. That makes rollback reconciliation quicker.
anya: Good. Who owns the runbook and automation? I'll volunteer to author the runbook and coordinate canary job with eng-sre.
jess: I'll wire up the console UI banners and dashboard card. Eva can you own telemetry counters and ingest-bot changes?
eva: Yep, I'll add the mismatch metric and the telemetry events. Will also push sampling config.
mike: I'll prototype projection materialized table and add sample SQL for index creation to the runbook.
rohan: I'll create the canary job and add the p95 auto-abort logic in the rollout controller.
ingest-bot: automated: scheduled shadow-write job will start at 2024-05-03T02:00Z if flags are set :gear:
anya: Thanks all. Next steps: I will draft the runbook PR today, assign owners, and request canary windows with SRE. If nobody objects, we'll schedule the dual-write enable for Tue morning. :eyes:
rohan: small nit — include a step to notify support via #support-alerts once canary reaches 20% so they can watch for customer tickets.
jess: added to runbook checklist.
mike: I'll drop the index DDL here when ready. For now noting: `CREATE INDEX ON ingestion_projection (route_id, day) WHERE day >= current_date - interval '14 days';`
anya: perfect. tagging this thread for follow-up. Thanks everyone.
